is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. coluzzii and An. gambiae s.s.) populations in Benin.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-West) and Ace-1 G119S (Ace-1R) in Table 2 and Table 3.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 and Table 3 provide genotype counts (e.g., 995F/F, 995F/L, 995L/L) and allele frequencies for each district and species.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field breeding sites in three districts in southern Benin (Porto-Novo, Akpro-Missérété, Lokossa).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical research study conducting field collections, bioassays, and molecular genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data at the district level (Porto-Novo, Akpro-Missérété, Lokossa) and includes coordinates in the Materials and Methods section.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study is published in 2026 and reports recent field collections (implied by the context of current resistance monitoring).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections and data analysis specific to this paper.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and bioassay results are provided in the main text tables and figures.

assessment.summary: This study assessed insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations from three districts in southern Benin. It found widespread pyrethroid resistance associated with near-fixation of the kdr L995F mutation, while Ace-1 G119S remained rare. Clothianidin and chlorfenapyr showed high efficacy.
